description: Low-precision FP8/BF16 trailing-update QR for the large n=2048/4096 shapes where the factor tolerance is loosest (~5e-3 to 1e-2). Blocked Householder with the two rank-nb trailing GEMMs in FP8-e4m3-in / FP32-accumulate (or BF16) tensor cores via cuBLASLt, panel and T-factor kept in FP32. One FP32 residual-correction sweep at the end to land inside 20*n*eps. Exploit B200 FP8 (~4500 TFLOPS, 2x BF16) on the most FLOP-heavy shapes.

BF16 trailing-update blocked Householder QR (nb=64) for n=2048/4096 + FP32 residual-correction sweep (R=triu(Q^T A)); off-grid and small/medium shapes -> geqrf. Validates (all guards clean). REGRESSION: correction sweep (householder_product + Q^T A) doubles the work; n=2048 132307us vs 77115 base (1.7x slower), n=4096 172989us vs 52227 (3.3x slower).

TF32 trailing update (allow_tf32) replaces BF16; closed-form compact-WY T via one triangular solve (I+diag(tau)triu(V^T V,1))T=diag(tau), eliminating the per-panel python j-loop. TF32 passes rankdef n=2048 directly (scaled 3.49<20) so the FP32 correction sweep is DROPPED. nb=64. Geomean 131944 (~baseline): n=2048 78601, n=4096 55146. Profile: panel geqr2 dominates ~90%.

nb=256 (divides 2048 and 4096 evenly; measured sweet spot from nb sweep {32..768}) + V-construction overhead trimmed (in-place unit diagonal, no torch.cat). TF32 trailing. Geomean 130038 (1.0086x over baseline 131153): n=2048 74129 (1.040x), n=4096 49702 (1.051x). Trailing precision (TF32/BF16/FP16) barely changes speed since the trailing update is only ~8-10% of time.

BEST: trial 3 (commit fdba2f0) = geomean 130038us (1.0086x over 131153 baseline). Low-precision trailing-update blocked Householder QR for n=2048/4096; other shapes -> geqrf. Per-shape: n=2048 B=8 74129us (1.040x over 77115), n=4096 B=2 49702us (1.051x over 52227). Validates fully (all 3 guards clean: diff-correctness, invariance, off-grid).

WHAT WORKED: (1) TF32 (allow_tf32) trailing GEMMs W=V^T C, C-=V(T^T W) with FP32 accumulate; orthogonality is ALWAYS ~1e-8 (Q=householder_product of FP32 reflectors is exactly orthogonal regardless of trailing precision), so only the FACTOR residual is at risk. TF32 keeps it well inside 20*n*eps for ALL conditioning at n>=2048 (rankdef n=2048 scaled 3.49<20), so the FP32 correction sweep was DROPPED (it doubled work -> trial 1 was 1.7-3.3x SLOWER). (2) Closed-form compact-WY T via ONE triangular solve (I+diag(tau)triu(V^TV,1))T=diag(tau), killing the per-panel python j-loop. (3) nb=256 (divides 2048&4096 evenly; swept {32..768}, 256 optimal).

THE CEILING (profile-confirmed, trial-3 nsys saved): the FP32 Householder PANEL factorization (cuSOLVER geqr2_smem_domino) is 92% of the time; the TF32 trailing GEMMs are <1% and the T-factor trsm is 6%. Measured: geqrf is PERFECTLY SERIAL over the batch (cost ratio = B exactly: 8.01x for B=8, 2.00x for B=2). So the low-precision trailing lever is real but capped at ~1.05x on these LOW-BATCH large-n shapes because the latency-bound serial panel dominates. Even at B=1 blocked-TF32 is only ~1.02x (n=4096) -- cuSOLVER's single-matrix geqrf already uses efficient trailing kernels. BF16/FP16 trailing = same speed as TF32 (trailing isn't the bottleneck), BF16 less accurate (sf 8.5 vs 1.2). FP8 (_scaled_mm, per-tensor scale) FAILED correctness (scaled ~100>>20; needs fine per-block scaling) AND was SLOWER (0.94x, batch-loop launch overhead) -- a measured negative for FP8 on these shapes.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not pursued here): (1) BATCHING THE PANEL is the whole game for n=2048 (serial 8x -> single-matrix ~9600us is an 8x floor) but cuSOLVER won't batch geqrf and CUDA streams are BANNED by the leaderboard guard; a CUSTOM batched-Householder panel kernel could batch it, though occupancy is poor at B=2/8 (2-8 CTAs of 148 SMs) -- worth measuring for n=2048 (B=8) specifically, not n=4096 (B=2, a single matrix already saturates the GPU). (2) The 6% T-factor trsm loops per-matrix in cuSOLVER -- a batched/custom T builder could shave it. (3) EXTENDING this exact TF32-blocked path to the large-BATCH shapes n=1024 (B=60) and n=512 (B=640) -- there the batched trailing GEMMs amortize far better and the serial-panel cuSOLVER weakness is the baseline's biggest cost; off MY brief's n=2048/4096 scope but the same code, and those shapes carry 9/12 of the geomean. (4) Per-block-scaled FP8 (brief's headline) only pays once the panel is batched and the trailing update becomes the bottleneck. REMOTE-SAFETY: this path is pure-PyTorch (no custom CUDA, no load_inline), so it avoids the BF16x9 remote-build failure mode; still recommend a leaderboard submit to confirm TF32 trailing is remote-safe before trusting it.
